articles.title: David Staff obituary
articles.summary: My former teacher and mentor David Staff, who has died aged 68 of a heart condition, was a cornetto player and period trumpeter, but also well known as a maker of natural trumpets – valveless brass instruments which, in the hands of a good player, produce a distinctive and rich sound.
body: The natural trumpet was the type of trumpet which, for many centuries, accompanied men and horses on the battlefield, but it was also admired by composers such as Bach and Handel, who both wrote music for it.

David got into making his instruments after meeting the natural trumpet maker Frank Tomes in the late 1980s. He learned a lot from Frank, and eventually became his apprentice in 2009, establishing his own workshop at his home near Coddenham in Suffolk. There he would make trumpets from flat sheets of brass: he shaped and soldered his tubes and drew them by hand, and created flared bell sections by hammering and swaging them into shape.

After Frank’s death David took over the business, with valuable input from his friend and fellow instrument maker, Graham Nicholson. Having served as David’s apprentice and hand engraver for 11 years, I will continue the workshop.

articles.title: Prince, the pope, and autumn 2026: purple is hot this season
articles.summary: Spotted on Balenciaga, Celine and Valentino catwalks, purple is having a moment. If you really want to stand out, wear it with red. The colour purple has links to royalty, the Catholic church, Prince, Gordon Brown’s ties and Barney the dinosaur and it now has a new association – autumn 2026.
body: It has been deemed fashion’s favourite colour having been spotted on autumn/winter catwalks, with Balenciaga, Celine and Valentino showcasing all-purple designs.

Jennifer Lawrence and Zoë Kravitz have also been spotted wearing purple, while Naomi Ackie and Nicola Peltz have worn it on the red carpet. The high street is in on the trend too, with Cos, H&M and Asos selling purple knitwear and accessories.

This season’s shade has been called “royal purple” – a vivid take on the colour, rather than a darker plum or muted lilac. This is a contrast to the neutrals that have dominated fashion in recent years.
In fact, fashion insiders are leaning into the bright theme by often pairing purple with red. Vogue recently declared that autumn’s “coolest colour clash” had arrived.

articles.title: Martine Rose appointed creative director at Balenciaga
articles.summary: Fashion house move marks breakthrough in white, male-dominated industry. For the first time in its 109-year history, the fashion house Balenciaga is to be led by a woman, with the British designer Martine Rose appointed as creative director of the brand.
body: Her appointment at Balenciaga marks a breakthrough in the white, male-dominated fashion industry. Rose is only the second Black woman to lead a major European house. Her appointment follows Grace Wales Bonner, who in 2025 was announced as the men’s creative director at Hermès.

Rose, who launched her own label in London in 2007, has become one of the most influential voices in menswear. She has built a cult following for her streetwear-inspired designs and celebrations of British subcultures through her mashup of influences including football, reggae and northern soul.

Her designs have been worn by celebrities including Justin Bieber, Timothée Chalamet and Drake. Alongside namechecking her in a song, the rapper Kendrick Lamar turned to Rose for a custom varsity jacket, emblazoned with Gloria, one of his song titles, for his widely acclaimed 2025 Super Bowl half-time performance. Rihanna and Hailey Bieber are also fans.
She succeeds Pierpaolo Piccioli, whose departure was announced on Thursday after 18 months at the luxury Spanish brand.
points: Fashion house move marks breakthrough in white, male-dominated industry.

articles.title: Autism, masking, and building a more inclusive world | Letters
articles.summary: Readers respond to an article by John Harris on the rise in the number of people labelled autistic over the last 20 years. John Harris’s article addresses all the main issues that are being debated around autism ( ‘The term is becoming unrecognisable’: have the experts who believed in a single…
body: From a young age I sensed that I was experiencing the world differently to other people. I was bullied, and worked hard to fit in. I was fortunate as structurally I had a stable life that mitigated some of the more challenging aspects of my life. Things started to get less manageable when I entered adulthood and left home.

Since the age of 25 I have experienced bouts of depression and ongoing anxiety, often resulting in breakdowns, or what I now understand to be autistic burnouts. Throughout adulthood I have seen numerous medical professionals and repeatedly been directed towards therapies, designed to deal with anxiety and depression, which have had limited success in addressing my life challenges.

Despite having a postgraduate education, I have struggled to hold down many jobs and have had to leave most due to stress. I have ongoing relationship problems. I don’t have children, partly due to reluctance and health issues. I suffer from fatigue and sleep issues.
points: Readers respond to an article by John Harris on the rise in the number of people labelled autistic over the last 20 years.

articles.title: Can Dubai Become the World's Fittest City?
articles.summary: This November marks the 10th annual Dubai Fitness Challenge, one of the largest community fitness initiatives in the world. Here's how visitors can join in on the fun.
body: At 6 a.m. on Sunday, November 22, Dubai 's Sheikh Zayed Road will fall silent. For one morning only, the city's six-lane superhighway—usually a blur of Nissan Patrols, taxis, and delivery scooters—will belong to tens of thousands of competitors as Dubai Run takes over the city’s skyline at dawn, following in the footsteps of a record 307,000 participants last year.

Leading the charge is usually Dubai's Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the driving force behind the Dubai Fitness Challenge (DFC) and one of the city's most ambitious experiments: to turn itself into the fittest city in the world.

"The people of Dubai have created an inspirational fitness movement, sending a powerful message that traveled far beyond our city,” Sheikh Hamdan said during a previous edition of the challenge. “Together, let us transform Dubai into the fittest city in the world.”

articles.title: Salma Hayek Pinault, Jane Fonda, and Hollywood’s Leading Names Gathered to Toast Women In Film
articles.summary: If there was one room in Hollywood where female power was unmistakable, it was the Beverly Hilton on Thursday night, where Women In Film hosted its annual WIF Honors.
body: Presented in partnership with Max Mara, the night brought together Salma Hayek Pinault, Kerry Washington, Jane Fonda, Olivia Munn, Emmy Rossum, Sharon Stone, and Katherine LaNasa. Naturally, Max Mara had plenty of representation in the room, with Fonda, Hannah Waddingham, Caylee Cowan, and breakthrough star Adria Arjona among those wearing the Italian label. Washington, meanwhile, opted for Balmain, while LaNasa chose Michael Kors.

One of the night’s standout moments came when Fonda took the stage to present Hayek Pinault with the Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award. It was a particularly fitting pairing, given their longstanding commitment to using their platforms to advocate for human rights and social issues. Reflecting on their shared history, Fonda recalled traveling to Mexico with Hayek Pinault more than two decades ago to raise awareness about hundreds of women and girls who had been murdered or declared missing.

articles.title: Where to Eat Gluten-Free in Montreal
articles.summary: Travel and food writer Luke Pyenson shares where to find the city’s best gluten-free bites, sips, and dining experiences.
body: Recently I’ve noticed more and more food people going to Montreal —and who can blame them? This laid-back bilingual gem on the St. Lawrence River is one of North America’s very best food cities. Personally I’ve loved it since my first visit almost 20 years ago. Montreal’s wonderful food scene draws me back year after year, sometimes multiple times,and by now the six-hour drive from my home in New York City feels like a breeze. It helps to know that my top meals of the year are waiting just across the border.

But for the past two years, following my wife’s celiac diagnosis, I have been navigating the city a little differently. When I was younger, trips to Montreal meant poutine, bagels, smoked-meat sandwiches, and a plethora of other canonical Québécois favorites that happen to be full of gluten. These days we prioritize other local favorites and have developed a dependable roster of businesses we trust—and that don’t feel like a compromise. Luckily there are a ton of them; we’ve been thrilled to discover that Montreal is a paradise for gluten-free eating.
points: Travel and food writer Luke Pyenson shares where to find the city’s best gluten-free bites, sips, and dining experiences.

articles.title: ChatGPT's New GIF Generator Is Fun, but Won't Replace Us Humans (Yet)
articles.summary: When it comes to generating AI images, both Gemini and ChatGPT do a passable job. In most cases, the results will look AI-generated, but they likely won’t have glaring spelling issues or missing limbs. Now, OpenAI is trying something new, introducing GIF support for ChatGPT.
body: OpenAI is pitching the new feature as an animation tool, not exactly as a way to create looping videos—though that’s how I ended up using it. You give ChatGPT a prompt, as detailed as you can make it, and the chatbot produces a GIF in just a few seconds. You can start with your own drawings or images, too. ChatGPT uses sketches as the base for animations, though it can turn any still image into animated GIFs. Like other AI editing tools, you can edit it if ChatGPT didn't quite get it right: You can ask ChatGPT to make the GIF longer or shorter, remove certain objects, change the style, slow down transitions, among other edits.

AI art can be quite sterile, but I was surprised by how adding motion and animation to the mix makes generating images a lot more fun. Unlike traditional GIFs, which usually pull from existing video clips, you can turn anything you want into a GIF, which is especially cool if you're using your own art. In my testing, I found this to be the most rewarding part. It’s not always possible to one-shot a GIF with a single prompt. But after a few rounds of edits, I ended up creating some GIFs that I actually wanted to share in my WhatsApp groups.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka, Coco Gauff, Mirra Andreeva, and More on Winning, Losing, Living, and Dreaming
articles.summary: With the WTA Finals about to kick off in Indian Wells, we gathered the top eight stars in women’s tennis to dish on their years and their lives.
body: Ahead of the season-ending WTA Finals tournament, kicking off Sunday at Indian Wells, the world’s eight highest-ranked women’s tennis players gathered for a fashion shoot and an easy hang. There, they talked exclusively to Vogue about their biggest wins, their toughest losses, their secret lives away from the court (pole dancing, UFC, baking cakes— who knew? )—and what they like to wear.
HEATED RIVALRY? Elina Svitolina, in Tom Ford, scores a snack while Rybakina, Gauff, and Muchova come away empty-handed.
The Indian Wells final was one of the best, because it was a really tough match, and I was a couple of match points down—I had to overcome a lot of things, and I got the win.

Obviously the Australian and US Open finals—in Australia [against Elena Rybakina], I had a break in the third set and felt like everything was going my way, but then it slipped, so I was really, really disappointed with that one. I should have won that one, but I didn’t. The US Open, not so much—[Rybakina] played really incredibly, and I didn’t.
